title: Repository build package and contract test governance
purpose: Record design-only governance for lockfile hygiene and contract test standards before UI or package graph expansion, without dependency changes, lockfile edits, validator implementation, test implementation, or readiness claims.

nonClaims: No readiness, staging, production, deployment, compliance, store, release, live-provider, or human-acceptance claim is made.

sourceReferences: workspace package manifests under apps, capabilities, adapters, and packages

workspace.interpretation: The workspace file declares future package roots for package-manager resolution only. These globs do not authorise creation of implementation directories, runtime code, package implementations, or readiness claims without an approved implementation directive.

packageGraph.interpretation: The current package graph is manifest-heavy and script-light: package manifests declare package names and export surfaces, while build, lint, typecheck, and test execution are routed at the repository root.

typescriptConfig.interpretation: The current TypeScript configuration is layered through a root config extending the base config, with no project references and no emitted build outputs configured at the repository TypeScript layer.

buildAndCacheSurface.interpretation: The inspected build/cache surface is currently package-manager and generated-Compose oriented. No Dockerfile or Compose build section was observed in the bounded scan, so Docker or Compose image build optimisation remains a future design and decision surface rather than an implemented build-cache surface.

rules: Treat package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, package manager version, workspace configuration, and relevant environment inputs as correctness-affecting package inputs.
Use frozen install semantics for validation and proof paths unless a later issue explicitly authorises a dependency update workflow.
A lockfile change must be tied to an intentional dependency, package-manager, override, or workspace change and must not be bundled with unrelated semantic edits.
Lockfile-only churn without package intent is a review evidence requirement until explained.
Cache keys for install or dependency outputs must include package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm version, workspace configuration, platform where relevant, and any dependency override file.
Supply-chain, SBOM, licence, and provenance outputs must be regenerated or invalidated when dependency inputs change.
Unknown dependency drift fails closed to frozen reinstall and full affected validation.

risk: dependency cache reuse can hide stale or unreviewed lockfile state
lockfile churn can obscure real dependency changes
package manager mismatch can make local and CI installs diverge

validationProofExpectation: Before implementation, compare cold and warm install behaviour where package changes are involved.
Strictly parse package metadata and preserve frozen install gates.
Invalidate SBOM, licence, provenance, dependency cache, and package proof artifacts on package or lockfile input changes.
Record dependency and cache decisions separately from semantic, validator, and runtime changes.

contractClasses.purpose: Prove machine-readable semantic artefacts retain strict shape, controlled values, and registry consistency.
Prove API contract surfaces and generated clients remain aligned before runtime or UI work depends on them.
Prove database type and query contract expectations remain aligned with declared schema or generated type surfaces.
Prove generated Compose outputs remain catalogue-driven and do not drift from service, port, profile, and hardening policy.
Prove provider-backed runtime behaviour is exercised at the lowest sufficient proof level and escalates to Compose when provider semantics matter.
Prove generated reports, proof artifacts, freshness, custody, and evidence references do not overclaim authority or status.

preserved: test speed cannot replace contract correctness
contract tests do not create readiness claims by themselves
generated clients and generated reports remain lower authority than the semantic or raw evidence surfaces they derive from
ambiguity falls back to fuller affected validation or proof
risk: contract tests can become theatrical if they only check generated output shape
contract tests can under-prove provider behaviour if in-memory checks are treated as provider proof
contract fixtures can drift if source, generated projection, and evidence references are not tied together

validationProofExpectation: Future implementation must define contract fixtures and negative controls before relying on a new contract gate.
Contract tests must fail closed on missing source reference, stale generated projection, provider-mode mismatch, environment mismatch, or unknown controlled value.
Contract tests must declare whether they are source, generated projection, provider, integration, or evidence contracts.
Fallback to full applicable gates on ambiguity.

pnpmWorkspaceReviewPolicy.workspaceShape: The current workspace declares apps, capabilities, adapters, and packages roots. The roots are treated as package-manager routing declarations, not semantic approval for implementation structure.
pnpmWorkspaceReviewPolicy.assuranceImpact: Workspace shape affects dependency resolution, install cache behaviour, package-boundary validation, and future contract-test routing. Unknown workspace impact must fall back to the full local foundation gate instead of narrowing validation scope.
validationProofExpectation: Cold and warm install evidence should be compared before claiming install-cache optimisation.
Package additions must trace to an approved implementation scope and must not be justified by workspace globs alone.
Cache keys must include package manifests, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, the package-manager version, overrides, and allow-build settings.
Unknown workspace impact, missing package-boundary evidence, or dependency-resolution drift must fail closed to full validation.

policyRules: Generated clients and build artifacts must trace to active source contracts and approved generator inputs, not to planned schemas by themselves.
Generation must be deterministic or explicitly record bounded non-determinism and its comparison rule.
Generated projections and generated reports are not semantic authority and cannot upgrade readiness claims.
Cache keys must include source contract hashes, schema lifecycle state, package-manager version, lockfile state, generator version, build configuration, and relevant environment dimensions.
UI or app-surface consumption requires source-to-output traceability, contract conformance evidence, and retained raw validation evidence.
Unknown source contracts, planned-only schema inputs, stale generated output, missing hashes, missing generator metadata, or lifecycle mismatch must fail closed.
generatedClientAndBuildArtifactPolicy.assuranceImpact: Generated clients and build artifacts are high-leverage integration surfaces. If their source contracts, hashes, lifecycle state, generator version, or cache keys drift, UI readiness and contract-test results can appear valid while no longer matching governed semantics.
validationProofExpectation: Generated outputs must prove reproducibility or record an explicit deterministic comparison exception.
Contract-conformance checks must compare generated clients against the governed source contract used to generate them.
Validation must fail stale output, missing source hash, schema lifecycle mismatch, unknown generator input, or missing retention evidence.
Evidence must preserve the distinction between raw validation evidence, generated artifacts, and generated reports.

pnpmStoreAndCachePolicy.assuranceImpact: The pnpm store and install cache are high-impact optimisation surfaces because stale dependency state can make validation, proof, generated clients, and supply-chain reports appear current when their dependency inputs have changed.
validationProofExpectation: Install-cache keys must include package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm version, overrides, allow-build settings, and platform where native builds can affect output.
Frozen install remains the default proof-preserving behaviour until an explicit dependency update workflow is authorised.
Dependency cache reuse must not bypass SBOM, licence, provenance, contract, or generated-artifact invalidation when package inputs change.
Unknown cache provenance or missing package input evidence must fail closed to reinstall and full affected validation.

observedState.interpretation: No package dependency name was observed with multiple declared ranges across dependency, development dependency, peer dependency, or optional dependency sections in the bounded package-manifest inspection.

dependencyDuplicationAudit.assuranceImpact: Duplicate dependency ranges can create non-deterministic install trees, larger lockfiles, divergent local and CI behaviour, and hidden generated-client or validator drift. The current inspection found no multiple-range dependency declaration that needs a consolidation decision in this issue.
validationProofExpectation: Future package additions should repeat duplicate-range inspection before claiming dependency hygiene remains preserved.
If duplicate ranges are introduced, consolidation requires an intentional dependency decision rather than silent lockfile churn.
Dependency duplication findings must remain separate from semantic authority and must not justify implementation changes by themselves.
